Hi all — attaching the operational sketch. High level notes:

- Private deployment (VPC) option: we support customer-supplied KMS/HSM (Bring Your Own Key) via standard Cloud KMS integrations or external HSM connectors (KMIP). In that mode customer keys are generated and stored in the customer's HSM/KMS and Redwood never has plaintext keys.
- Redwood-managed KMS: keys are generated in our HSM-backed KMS and wrapped with tenant-scoped encryption; Redwood can rotate keys on schedule and provide key-handle logs.
- For the UK addendum/TIA: auditors typically ask for key custody evidence (rotation policy, key manifest, KMS audit logs). We can provide redacted KMS audit exports and a signed attestation for retention/rotation.

See attached: kms-keystore-sequence.png (diagram) — shows both BYOK and Redwood-managed flows and where tokenization/prefix caching occurs in the serving runtime.

Logan

Hi Lena — quick legal note:

- Redwood executes our standard DPA and we attach the UK Addendum when the customer requests UK-specific language. In my experience this is functionally equivalent to an IDTA for most auditors; we do not routinely ask customers to sign a separate bespoke UK IDTA unless there are unusual contractual constraints (e.g., cross-border escrow clauses).
- If EuroHealth requires a signed UK IDTA clause (vs addendum), we can provide a signable cover sheet that mirrors the Addendum's obligations but we will need a standard counterparty signature path (DocuSign).
- Regarding evidence: we can provide the TIA packet (scope, key custody docs, subprocessor list, network flow diagrams, and redacted audit logs). We will redline anything that would reveal other customers.

If you can confirm the likely deployment model and whether legal would accept the Addendum as-is, I will prepare the Addendum + a one-page summary for your auditors.

Kind regards,
